children.text: A city park of about 32.84 hectares in the heart of Baguio. Lake boats, bicycles, the Rose Garden and Igorot Garden sit in one place, making it an easy free half day, and the lake reopened on
September 1, 2026
Burnham Park is an urban park of about 32.84 hectares on the flat basin floor of downtown Baguio. American city planner Daniel Burnham conceived it as the green heart of Baguio in his
city plan, and the park carries his surname. The area is said to have been a damp basin the Ibaloi people called "Kafagway," and it was set aside as a park reservation by Proclamation No. 64 on
August 6, 1925
. Today a bust of Burnham still greets visitors beside the Rose Garden at the north entrance.
The heart of the park is Burnham Lake, a man-made lake. It covers about 4 hectares and is said to average about
3m

in depth, with boat docks, promenades and bike paths along its edge. Pines and weeping willows ring the lake and broad plazas cross the park paths, and the cool highland air keeps a walk comfortable even at midday.

The park is not one block but a chain of zones. The Rose Garden at the north entrance, Igorot Garden honoring the Igorot people, the Orchidarium full of orchids, the children's playground, the skating rink, the football field and athletics track (the Athletic Bowl), and the Melvin Jones Grandstand that hosts big events each have their own mood. With no entrance fee and easy access by jeepney, taxi or on foot, it is the easiest sight to reach in Baguio.
The lake closed for rehabilitation on
October 1, 2025
and reopened about 11 months later, on
September 1, 2026

, Baguio's Charter Day. New boats, new docks and lakeside seating have been added, while the Rose Garden, children's park and skating rink await the next phase of work. It suits early-morning walkers, families who want to ride bikes and boats with children, and travelers who want to rest for half a day in the middle of the city.
Rent a swan-shaped pedal boat or a wooden rowboat and circle the lake. The fare set by Baguio city is
per boat for
30 minutes
or
for
1 hour
, regardless of boat size. A boat is said to carry four to five passengers besides the rower, so it works well for families.
On the flat paths linking the lakeside and plazas you can rent single bikes, sidecar bikes for 2–4 people, and pedal karts. Rental costs roughly
for
30 minutes to 1 hour
depending on type, and families make up many of the visitors.
This northern zone near the gate leads to the Burnham bust and the stairway toward City Hall. The roses are at their fullest from
November to February
, and at year's end long beds are sometimes filled with red poinsettias.

blocks.title: Igorot Garden and the Freedom Monument

children.text: A small garden at one side of the park holds the bronze Cordillera Freedom Monument, which depicts five Igorot warriors. The work of sculptor Toym Imao, it was unveiled in
and symbolizes the pride of Cordillera's Indigenous peoples, making it a popular photo spot.

The western zone has the Orchidarium, which gathers highland orchids in cool shade, and a children's playground. The play equipment is said to have been replaced a few years ago, so it is a fine place to rest with children.
The skating rink lies south of the lake. Use is said to cost about
per person, and since this area is due for work in the next phase, it is best to check on site whether it is open.

blocks.title: Melvin Jones Grandstand and the Athletic Bowl

children.text: A large grandstand and sports ground on the southeast side near Harrison Road. Football practice, performances and civic events are held here, and the parade of the
February
Panagbenga flower festival ends here.
From
6 a.m. to 9 a.m.
you will see locals jogging and strolling beside a quiet lake. The sun is mild and crowds are thin, so it is the best time for photos.

Victory Liner, Genesis and Solid North buses run several times a day from PITX, Pasay and Cubao in Manila. As of August 2026, regular air-conditioned buses cost about
, deluxe and JoyBus-class about
, and first-class and luxury about
Via TPLEX the trip takes
5–6 hours
. On weekends, holidays and during Panagbenga it can stretch to
7–9 hours
, so allow extra time.
From the Baguio terminal to Burnham Park a taxi costs about
. If you arrive by air, the closest option is to land at Clark International Airport (CRK) and transfer to a bus.
Drive up via NLEX–SCTEX–TPLEX; it takes about
4–6 hours
from Manila. Kennon Road is often closed for rockfalls or repairs, so consider the Marcos Highway route first.
Parking near the park is said to be strictly time-limited. Fees run about
depending on place and time, and long-term parking may be enforced against, so check the signs on site.
Baguio's Loakan Airport resumed scheduled service on a Cebu route in
December 2022
but it was suspended in
July 2024
. Check airline and Civil Aviation Authority (CAAP) notices first for whether scheduled passenger flights operate now; if not, go by bus from Clark.
From Session Road, Baguio Cathedral and SM City Baguio it is a downhill walk of
5–10 minutes
to the park. The way back is uphill, so consider a taxi or jeepney.
Jeepneys cost about
on most stretches, and city taxis run about
for short rides. Always ask the driver to switch on the meter.
Because this is an outdoor park, the weather shapes how much you enjoy it. Baguio's average annual temperature is about
, and in the
November–April
dry season it is clear and cool, the best time for the lake and a loop by bike. The Rose Garden is at its fullest from
November to February
. The Panagbenga flower festival takes place in
February
; in
it ran from
February 1
to
March 8
, and the parade route ends at the Melvin Jones Grandstand beside the park. A flower market sometimes sets up near the park's skating rink during this period.
March–May
is hot but clear peak season, especially crowded during Holy Week. In the
June–October

rainy season afternoon showers and thick fog are frequent, and when a typhoon passes hundreds of millimeters of rain can fall in a day. In heavy rain you may not be able to take a boat and the lawns can turn muddy, so finish your plans early in the morning and bring a raincoat. Panagbenga dates change every year, so check the latest announcements.

The park is downtown, so it is close to almost any lodging. Hotels along Harrison Road and the lower end of Session Road are within walking distance of the park and near the bus terminal and market. This area is convenient for morning walks, with guesthouses at about
per night and mid-range hotels at about
. Prices rise sharply and rooms fill early during Panagbenga and Holy Week, so book ahead.
Inside the park, stalls sell street snacks such as strawberry taho (about
), and Solibao on Lake Drive south of the lake is a Filipino home-cooking restaurant that has operated since

. At dusk a night market sets up on Harrison Road beside the park, where you can eat grilled food and street food, and if you walk up to Session Road there are many old bakeries and cafes. If hygiene worries you, use licensed kiosks and restaurants.
The best time is on a weekday,
6 a.m. to 9 a.m.
. You avoid the crowds and midday sun and can see the morning scene reflected in the lake.
The park itself is free and open around the clock, but boat and bike rentals usually run from about
until around
6 p.m.
Most vendors take cash only, so carry plenty of small bills such as
and
Confirm the fare before boarding, ask for an official receipt, and put life jackets on children first.
Check the brakes and seat before renting a bike, and slow down on a sidecar bike when children are aboard.
On weekend mornings the boat line can run
15–20 minutes
, so a weekday morning is easier for family trips.
Even if midday feels mild, mornings and evenings are chilly, so bring a light jacket.
During Panagbenga the roads around the park are closed, so walking is faster than a taxi.
Boat fares are still unsettled just after the reopening. The city insisted that only
may be charged for 30 minutes, yet some operators demanded
or more. Confirm the fare before you board.
Swimming in the lake is prohibited. The average depth is about
3m
, so never let go of a child's hand on a boat.
Pickpockets can operate on crowded days. Keep your phone and wallet in a bag worn in front.
The Rose Garden, children's park and skating rink are ahead of the next phase of work, so some sections may be closed off or changed. Follow the barriers and signs and check the latest announcements.
Littering is subject to enforcement, with fines said to run around
. Use the designated bins.
At night, avoid quiet corners and stay on the broad central paths and lit areas.
Right after the reopening, reports said only 2 of the 9 boat operators met the new boat standards. Avoid old boats and check that life jackets are worn.
Session Road, the public market and Baguio Cathedral cluster within a
5–10 minute
walk of the park.
